Reference forearm is a plain cylinder. Put maximum circumference in the upper third and bring the wrist to roughly 60% of it. The cuff-link-wrist transition is a black-tie signature and needs a real wrist to sit on; on a cylinder the French cuff reads as a bracelet.

do_not_copy: The slab torso: roughly 0.75 head-heights of chest depth with near-parallel front and back planes. the reference buys all its breadth in the frontal plane and none in depth. River's three-quarter table cameras will expose this immediately.
The undersized hand at 0.55-0.60 of head height. Unacceptable in a game whose entire verb set is performed by hands.
Fingertips landing at the upper third of the thigh instead of mid-thigh — the short-forearm read.
The crotch line sitting slightly below mid-height (long torso, short leg). River sets it at 50-51%.
The no-neck yoke: a very short visible neck column plus a steep unbroken trapezius sweep from mastoid to acromion with no trap/deltoid plane break.
The straight lower back and neutral-to-posterior pelvic tilt in profile. It becomes a slump the moment the character sits down.
Smooth featureless clavicle tubes with no S-curve or acromial termination, and a chest that reads as one continuous plane from collar to belt with no pectoral shelf.
The perfectly cylindrical forearm with no brachioradialis swell and no taper into the wrist.
The build slider behaviour recorded in the manifest — torso mass changes while limbs stay fixed. Anything River exposes must co-vary limb circumference with torso mass.
The cargo-shorts hip flare read as body width. That is a garment silhouette, not anatomy; do not bake it into the base mesh.
The late taper that keeps the ribcage near full shoulder width all the way down to the belt. River's taper starts at the lower pectoral.

Any absolute male/female height ratio derived from the two full-body frames. The manifest calls them directly comparable, but the male fills roughly 860px of frame height against the female's roughly 560px — the subject distance differs, so only internal ratios are trustworthy.
pitfalls: Widening the shoulders without deepening the chest. The most common way to make a game male look 'built', and it produces a torso that is convincing dead-on and cardboard at three-quarter — which is River's default camera.
Reaching for the muscle macro to get mass. It reads as bodybuilder, not Bond lead, and it fights the dinner jacket. Mass belongs in skeletal breadth and ribcage depth with muscle held low.

Locking heights uniform, then also matching limb circumferences by inertia. The male and female silhouettes converge and the only remaining difference is the head and the costume — which defeats the whole point of spending the dimorphism budget on mass.
Thickening the neck without lengthening the visible column. Gives the football-player read; black tie cannot carry it, and the wing collar loses its landing.
Enlarging the head to improve readability at table distance. Instant caricature. Hold 7.75-8.0 heads and solve legibility with silhouette and value contrast.

Sculpting and judging the proportions standing. Seated at the table the visible content is head, neck, shoulder yoke, upper arm, forearm and hands — thigh and calf mass are nearly invisible. Shoulder-to-waist, neck, and hand size do all the work. Check every delta in the seated pose before accepting it.

Pushing the V-taper deep on the naked body and then adding a structured jacket on top. The tailoring should carry most of the apparent shoulder width; an already-extreme body plus a roped sleevehead lands in superhero.

Trusting the manifest's 'same camera, same lens' claim for absolute measurements. The stance and garment match; the subject distance does not. Ratios internal to each figure are sound, cross-figure absolutes are not.
Correcting arm reach by lengthening the upper arm. The reference upper arm is fine; the deficit is forearm plus hand. Lengthening the wrong segment breaks elbow placement on every table-contact pose.

Fixing hand size on the mesh but leaving the rig's hand bones and card/chip prop scales at the old ratio. A hand scaled 25% up has to propagate to grip poses, card fan width and chip stack diameter or every prop contact goes wrong.
Adding a lumbar curve for the standing silhouette without checking it against the seated hip flexion. Overdone lordosis reads as an arched, posing stance when the character sits back in the chair.

Chasing anatomical description (clavicle S-curve, pectoral edge, brachioradialis) hard enough to cross into photoreal. These should be plane changes readable at silhouette scale, not gym-cut detail — River is slightly more grounded than the reference, not a different genre.

observations.feature: Spine angle from vertical at neutral rest
observations.reference_shows: The torso line from sacrum to acromion inclines forward roughly 15-20 degrees off vertical. The bend is at the femoral head: pelvis is tipped forward on the seat pan, the lumbar keeps a shallow forward curve, and there is no crease or fold at the waist. The chair back is 80-120 mm behind the shoulders and is not touched. Buttocks sit on the rear two-thirds of the seat pan with the pan's front edge under the mid-thigh.
observations.river_direction: Author River's neutral at 12-15 degrees from vertical — one notch more upright than the reference, because a Bond lead reads as composed, not settled-in. Keep the hinge exclusively at the hip joint; lock zero waist flexion in the neutral. Keep the pelvis back on the pan and let the sit bones contact and deform the cushion; the shoulder-to-chair-back gap should be 60-100 mm, present but never large enough to read as hovering.

observations.feature: Forearm-to-rail contact point and elbow angle
observations.reference_shows: Both forearms cross the leather rail at roughly the mid-forearm, about 40-45 percent of forearm length up from the wrist crease. The wrists clear the rail's inner roll so the hands sit over the felt edge, not on the rail's crown. The elbow points sit outside the rail's outer edge and below the rail top by roughly 30-50 mm — the elbows are not weight-bearing; the forearm mid-shaft carries the load. Included elbow angle reads about 95-110 degrees.
observations.river_direction: Match the contact geometry exactly: mid-forearm on the rail, wrist past the inner roll, elbow floating just outside and below. Author the elbow at 100-105 degrees. Add real contact deformation — the dinner-jacket sleeve should flatten and pucker where it crosses the rail edge, which is the single cheapest cue that stops a seated character reading as hovering.

observations.reference_shows: The forearms form a triangle: elbows sit roughly 1 to 1.5 hand-widths outside the ribcage silhouette on each side, and the forearms converge inward to meet at the body midline. From the front camera the elbows are the widest point of the whole character, wider than the shoulders.
observations.river_direction: Keep the converging triangle but pull the elbows in to about 0.75 hand-width outside the ribcage. the reference's wide diamond reads bar-casual; a tighter triangle reads club. This also matters practically — at a 9-seat ring the reference elbow width will clip the neighbouring seat's silhouette from the default seat camera.

observations.reference_shows: Acromion sits at or below its standing-rest height in every seated frame — no shrug anywhere in the set. The shoulders are rolled forward: the deltoid apex sits ahead of the frontmost point of the ribcage, with roughly 10-15 degrees of scapular protraction. The trapezius line from neck to shoulder point is long and shallow.
observations.river_direction: Keep the lowered acromion — that is the strongest single reason the reference reads planted rather than posed. Cut the protraction to 5-8 degrees. the reference's roll plus its forward head reads slumped; River's lead needs the same low shoulder with the chest plane still facing forward, so the collarbones stay near-horizontal rather than wrapping.

observations.reference_shows: The head is carried forward of the shoulder line — the ear canal sits ahead of the acromion by roughly half a head-width. The chin drops about 10-15 degrees so the gaze lands on the felt 250-350 mm in front of the seat, not at the table centre. In the two-player frame the same character props the chin on the back of a curled hand, head tipped an extra 5-8 degrees toward that hand.
observations.river_direction: Bring the ear back over the acromion, or ahead of it by no more than a quarter head-width, and cut the chin drop to 5-8 degrees. Aim the gaze at the community-card zone rather than at the near felt. The chin-on-hand variant is worth authoring as a secondary idle — it is the most character-carrying pose in the whole seated set — but with the fingers curled and the jaw resting on the proximal phalanges, not the palm.

observations.feature: Knee height relative to the table and femur slope
observations.reference_shows: The thigh slopes downhill from hip to knee — the knee sits roughly one thigh-diameter (about 100 mm) below the hip joint, because the chair pan is high relative to the rail. The rail's outer edge passes above the knee with clearance; the knee is genuinely under the table, not jammed against it. The shin drops close to vertical, heel roughly under or slightly behind the knee, foot flat on the floor.
observations.river_direction: Reproduce the downhill femur — a level or uphill thigh is what makes a seated rig look like it is perched on a stool. Hold 60-80 mm of vertical clearance between the knee's top surface and the rail underside so the lean-in extreme does not drive the thigh through the table. Feet flat with full sole contact and toes turned out 10-15 degrees each; a black patent oxford needs the sole plane visibly parallel to the floor.

observations.source_frame: 08_seated_posture/seated_profile_two_players_side.png (male gent right, female braided player left) and seated_lean_in_both_arms_on_table.png
observations.reference_shows: The male figures sit with the femora abducted roughly 10-15 degrees each side, so outside-of-knee to outside-of-knee spans about 1.3-1.4 times hip width. Elbows sit outside the torso silhouette. Upper-arm and deltoid mass carries the outer edge of the seated shape, so the widest horizontal line is at the elbows. The female player in the same frame keeps the femora near parallel, knees close, and her elbows track much closer to the ribcage, so her widest line is at the hips.
observations.river_direction: For silver: knees apart at 12 degrees abduction per side, elbows outside the ribcage, shoulder-and-elbow band carrying the widest horizontal read. This is the axis on which he must differ from the gold female — she should keep knees near-together or angled as a pair and elbows tucked, so her widest line stays at the hip and the shoulder tapers in. Do not attempt the distinction through mesh mass alone; it lives in the pose.

observations.feature: What the hands actually do at rest
observations.reference_shows: The hands are NOT interlaced. The right hand lies palm-down across the back of the left, fingers of the top hand crossing the lower hand at roughly 30 degrees, both sets of fingers relaxed and slightly curled with the fingertip pads touching the rail leather. The stack sits on the body midline. In the profile frames the same rest state is asymmetric instead — one hand cupped loosely over the hole card, the other raised to the chin or resting at the chip stack.
observations.river_direction: Author the hand-over-hand stack as River's neutral: cleaner and cheaper than an interlaced clasp, and it avoids the finger interpenetration that kills a low-poly clasp. Then author at least one asymmetric alternate — near hand cupped over the hole cards, far hand at the chip stack or the cuff link. Never leave the arms unsupported at the sides; the reference frame that does this (seated_neutral_arms_at_sides) is exactly the read River must avoid.

observations.reference_shows: Each finger is close to a constant-diameter cylinder for two-thirds of its length, then rounds off at the tip. There is almost no proximal-to-distal taper, no knuckle-crease indication, and no swell at the PIP joints. The little finger is noticeably shorter, its tip landing at about the ring finger's DIP. Nails are small, flat, pale quads with no nail-bed curvature.
observations.river_direction: Give River real taper — proximal phalanx roughly 15 percent wider than the distal, with a small diameter swell at the PIP and DIP so the finger reads as jointed rather than extruded. Keep the same little-finger length ratio; it is correct. Add nail-bed curvature and a slightly warmer nail-fold tone. This is the highest-value single upgrade in the hand, because at the seat camera the hands sit in the near foreground and the fingers are the largest readable detail on the character.

observations.reference_shows: The thumb root is a single soft rounded wedge. There is no separation between the thenar eminence and the first dorsal interosseous, and no hollow in the snuffbox. Thumb abduction at full spread reads about 65-70 degrees from the index axis; the web between thumb and index stretches as a flat sheet rather than folding.
observations.river_direction: Model the thenar as two masses with a shallow valley between the thenar pad and the first dorsal interosseous, and put a soft hollow at the base of the extensor tendons. Build the thumb web with enough spare geometry that at 60-plus degrees of abduction it folds along a crease instead of stretching to a paddle.

observations.feature: Knuckle read on the back of the hand
observations.reference_shows: The MCP row reads as one continuous soft ridge, not four distinct heads. There is zero extensor-tendon relief on the dorsum even with the fingers fully spread, and no visible ulnar head or wrist narrowing — the forearm flows into the hand as a single tapering tube.
observations.river_direction: Break the MCP ridge into four resolvable heads with shallow valleys between, and add two to three extensor tendon ridges on the dorsum that only surface when the fingers extend. Put in a genuine wrist: narrow the forearm at the wrist crease by about 20 percent from the forearm's widest, and read the ulnar head as a small bump on the little-finger side. In a dinner jacket the wrist is where the shirt cuff terminates, so this junction is on camera on every hand pose.

observations.feature: Hand and forearm scale relative to the head
observations.reference_shows: With both hands raised beside the face, each hand spans nearly the full cheek-to-cheek width of the head, and the palm reads almost as wide as it is long. The forearms are heavy, evenly cylindrical, and show no brachioradialis bulge or ulnar edge — cartoon slabs in short sleeves.
observations.river_direction: Bring the hand down to a credible ratio — wrist crease to middle fingertip roughly equal to chin-to-hairline, and palm width about 0.8 of palm length so the hand reads long rather than square. River's forearms are covered by the dinner-jacket sleeve to the wrist, so their silhouette is cloth: model the sleeve as a tapering tube with a break at the elbow and a cuff that stops 10-15 mm short of the shirt link, and put the anatomy budget into the hand instead.

observations.reference_shows: At full reach the torso pitches forward from the hip to about 30-35 degrees from vertical, the elbows open to roughly 150-160 degrees, and the hands land palm-down on the felt about a third of the way across, near the community-card line. Contact is at the hands only — the forearms leave the rail entirely. The shoulders stay LOW even at maximum reach; only the scapulae protract. The palms are flat and splayed on the felt with fingers together.
observations.river_direction: Keep the hip-hinge, the low shoulder and the hands-only contact; those are the reasons the reference reads weight-bearing. Cap River's lean at 25-28 degrees from vertical and stop the elbows at 145 degrees — the reference's near-straight arm plus flat splayed palm reads like shoving a table. Land River's fingers slightly curled with the fingertip pads and the hypothenar taking the weight, palm arch just clear of the felt.

observations.feature: Card-protect gesture and required finger spread
observations.source_frame: 08_seated_posture/seated_profile_forearms_on_rail.png (cream gent, near hand over the hole card) and seated_profile_two_players_side.png
observations.reference_shows: When a player covers a hole card the fingers are only slightly parted — well short of the maximum spread in the celebration frame. The hand cups over the card with the palm arch above it and the fingertips down on the felt, index and little finger straddling the card's short edges. A standard card is about 63 mm wide, so the index-to-little span needed is small.
observations.river_direction: Rig for about 15-20 degrees of MCP abduction at card-protect with the thumb abducted 30-35 degrees to sit against the card's near edge — and separately support 40-45 degrees MCP and 65-70 degrees thumb as the rig maximum for the win-reaction spread. Author the protect pose so the palm actually touches the back of the card rather than tenting above it; the tented version is the standard rig tell at this camera distance.

observations.feature: Camera caution on the reference frames
observations.reference_shows: Both frames named 'profile' in the manifest are actually raised orbit three-quarter views, roughly 25-35 degrees above the table plane and 20-30 degrees off true lateral. The apparent spine angle and thigh slope are therefore foreshortened, and the two frames disagree with each other by several degrees on the same character.
observations.river_direction: Treat every angle taken from these frames as a range, not a measurement. Set River's neutral in Blender against a true orthographic side view and validate it back against the reference by silhouette relationships — knee below rail, wrist past the inner roll, ear over acromion — rather than by matching a traced angle.

build_deltas.rationale: the reference's hand spans nearly the full cheek-to-cheek head width with a near-square palm. Pulling scale down until wrist-crease-to-middle-fingertip equals chin-to-hairline is what separates a credible male hand from the reference's cartoon paddle, and the hands sit in the near foreground of the default seat camera on every frame.

build_deltas.parameter: Palm width relative to palm length (hand-fingers-distance / palm proportion)
build_deltas.rationale: Reference palm reads roughly as wide as it is long. Target about 0.8 width-to-length so the hand reads long and tailored rather than blunt, which is the whole difference between a club silhouette and a bar one at rest on the rail.

build_deltas.parameter: Finger diameter taper, proximal to distal (hand-fingers-diameter)
build_deltas.rationale: Reference fingers are constant-diameter cylinders. Making the distal phalanx roughly 15 percent narrower than the proximal, with small swells at PIP and DIP, is the highest-value hand upgrade — it is what makes a finger read as jointed at gameplay distance.

build_deltas.parameter: Wrist circumference relative to forearm (wrist scale)
build_deltas.rationale: The reference forearm flows into the hand with no narrowing at all. Narrowing the wrist by about 20 percent from the forearm's widest creates a real wrist, and in black tie the shirt cuff and link terminate exactly there, so it is on camera in every hand pose.

build_deltas.parameter: Knuckle and dorsal tendon relief (hand surface detail)
build_deltas.rationale: The reference MCP row is a single soft ridge with zero extensor-tendon relief. Four resolvable knuckle heads plus two to three tendon ridges that surface only on extension put River a step past the reference without approaching photoreal skin detail.

Reference thumb root is one undifferentiated wedge with a stretching web. A shallow valley between the two masses plus a snuffbox hollow lets the web fold along a crease at 60-plus degrees of abduction instead of going paddle-shaped in the win reaction.

build_deltas.parameter: Shoulder width / deltoid mass (macro proportions plus upper-arm muscle)
build_deltas.rationale: The seated male read comes from the shoulder-and-elbow band carrying the widest horizontal line, versus the female's widest line at the hip. A slight increase over neutral is enough — it must not tip into superhero mass, and the dinner jacket's shoulder construction will add apparent width on top.

The reference's long shallow trap line is correct and is part of why the lowered acromion reads as composure rather than slump. Slightly less trap bulk than neutral keeps the neck long, which is what stops the low-shoulder pose reading as beaten.

Reference forearms are heavy even cylinders, but River's silver wears a jacket sleeve to the wrist, so the forearm silhouette is cloth. Spend nothing here; the budget belongs in the hand and the sleeve break.

build_deltas.parameter: Hip flexion in the neutral seated pose (pose parameter, not a morph)
build_deltas.rationale: Reference sits at 15-20 degrees from vertical. River's neutral at 12-15 degrees reads one notch more composed while keeping the hinge at the femoral head. Waist flexion stays at exactly zero — folding at the waist is what makes a seated character look boneless.

build_deltas.parameter: Scapular protraction in the neutral seated pose (pose parameter)
build_deltas.rationale: Reference rolls the shoulders forward 10-15 degrees so the deltoid apex sits ahead of the ribcage. Cutting to 5-8 degrees keeps the chest plane facing forward and the collarbones near-horizontal, which is the Bond read; the lowered acromion itself must be kept.

build_deltas.parameter: Forward head translation in the neutral seated pose (pose parameter)
build_deltas.rationale: Reference carries the ear half a head-width ahead of the acromion with a 10-15 degree chin drop, which reads slouched. Bringing the ear back over the acromion with a 5-8 degree chin drop, gaze on the community-card zone, is the difference between studying the felt and owning the table.

build_deltas.parameter: Femoral abduction (knee spread) in the neutral seated pose (pose parameter)
build_deltas.rationale: 12 degrees per side, giving an outside-knee span of about 1.3 times hip width, is the primary axis on which the silver male seated silhouette must differ from the gold female's near-parallel knees. It cannot be achieved through mesh mass.

build_deltas.parameter: Elbow lateral offset from the ribcage in the neutral seated pose (pose parameter)
build_deltas.rationale: Reference elbows sit 1 to 1.5 hand-widths outside the ribcage and are the widest point of the character. Pulling to about 0.75 hand-width tightens the converging forearm triangle to a club read and prevents silhouette collision with the neighbouring seat at a 9-seat ring.

build_deltas.parameter: Elbow flexion at neutral rail contact (pose parameter)
build_deltas.rationale: The reference's 95-110 degrees with the mid-forearm on the rail and the wrist past the inner roll is correct and load-bearing. Author River at 100-105 degrees and keep the elbow point floating 30-50 mm below the rail top rather than resting on it.

do_not_copy: Oversized hands — the reference hand spans nearly the whole head width with a near-square palm. River's must come down a full size and read long rather than blunt.

The wristless forearm-into-hand tube. There is no narrowing at the wrist crease and no ulnar head anywhere in the reference; in black tie the shirt cuff terminates exactly at that junction, so the absence would be conspicuous.
Constant-diameter finger cylinders with no PIP/DIP swell, no joint creases and no phalangeal taper.
The single soft MCP ridge with zero extensor-tendon relief on the back of the hand, even at full finger spread.
Shallow finger webs that ride high toward the PIP and stretch flat instead of folding when the fingers spread.

The forward-head-plus-rolled-shoulder combination. The lowered acromion is right and must be kept; the 10-15 degree protraction with the ear half a head-width ahead of the shoulder is a slouch and is wrong for a Bond lead.

Elbows parked 1 to 1.5 hand-widths outside the ribcage as a permanent state — it reads bar-casual and, at a 9-seat ring, collides with the neighbouring player's silhouette from the default seat camera.
The full-reach pose's near-straight arm (150-160 degrees) with flat splayed palms pressed on the felt. It reads like shoving furniture, not like reaching for cards.

Bare short-sleeved forearms as the source of the arm read. River's silver is sleeved to the wrist; the arm silhouette is tailoring, and the reference gives no useful information about sleeve behaviour at the rail.
The seated_neutral_arms_at_sides variant — unsupported arms hanging beside the body at a poker table. It is precisely the A-pose-adjacent read the River rule forbids.
Flat pale rectangular fingernails with no nail-bed curvature or nail-fold tone shift.
Mirrored, perfectly symmetric hand placement. Even the reference breaks symmetry in the profile frames, and symmetric hands are the loudest rig-default tell.
pitfalls: A-pose residue: arms authored at the sides or drifting toward the body when a hand-driven state has no defined pose. Every seated state must terminate with the hands on the rail, on the felt, or on the face.

Hovering. The classic failures are hands resting on the rail plane but floating 10-20 mm above it, buttocks not deforming the seat cushion, and soles not fully contacting the floor. Contact deformation on the jacket sleeve at the rail edge is the cheapest fix and the one most often skipped.

Folding at the waist instead of the hip. It kills the weight read instantly and makes the character look like it is sitting on the chair rather than in it — the reference gets this right and it is the single most transferable thing in the set.

Thigh-through-rail collision at the lean-in extreme. With the knee under the table there is only 60-80 mm of clearance, and a low-poly thigh with linear skinning will punch through the rail underside before the lean reaches its cap.
Elbow silhouette blowout. At a 9-seat ring the elbows are the widest part of a seated male; author the neutral tight or the character will overlap its neighbour on the default seat camera.

Fingers modelled at rest and then spread by the rig alone. The webs stretch, the palm goes paddle-shaped, and the win-reaction close-up is exactly where that gets seen. Build spare geometry into the webs and validate at 45 degrees MCP abduction.
Card-protect authored as a tent — palm arched clear of the card instead of touching its back. At the seat camera the gap reads as the hand not knowing where the card is.
Interlaced-finger clasp attempted at low poly. Fingers interpenetrate under any wrist rotation. The reference's hand-over-hand stack avoids the problem entirely and should be River's neutral.

Erasing the male/female distinction by reusing one seated pose. The read lives in knee spread, elbow width and where the widest horizontal line sits — not in mesh mass. Silver and gold sharing a pose will make both look wrong.

Over-correcting toward photoreal in the hand. Knuckle heads, tendon ridges and wrist narrowing are the step past the reference; pore detail, vein networks and prominent tendons on the neutral rest hand overshoot the thesis and fight the flat game lighting.
Losing the lowered shoulder while fixing the slouch. Raising the acromion to correct the forward head is the wrong lever — the shoulder must stay down; only the head and the protraction move.

Chasing traced angles from the two 'profile' frames. Both are raised orbit three-quarters and disagree with each other by several degrees on the same character; set the pose in an orthographic side view and validate by silhouette relationships instead.

synthesis.headline: The silver male is a credible late-thirties skull under black tie, read at three-quarter from across a dark table — so almost every decision is a value-and-silhouette decision before it is an anatomy decision. Masculinity must be earned forward and in planes, never laterally: brow projection with a broken slab, a real nasion scoop, forward malar over a shallow hollow with the masseter behind it, a gonial corner that is unmistakable in silhouette but sits inside the temple width, and a chin that comes forward as it narrows. Everything the reference hides behind a beard, a bright grey backdrop or a moulded hair shell has to be genuinely built here, because River's lead is clean-shaven, lit dark, and framed large in the preview bust and the winner close-up. Two of the three highest-value surfaces are material, not geometry: a dinner-suit contract (floor the cloth at 4-5% reflectance, hard roughness split between barathea and satin, authored seam AO, a weave that survives the real texel density) and an eye contract (globe set back, upper lid crossing the top of the iris, tinted sclera with lid occlusion). The third is the hands — it is a poker game, they sit nearest camera on every deal, and their scale is the one number the readers actively disagree about. Finally, he shares a skeleton, a height and a pipeline with the gold female, so the male read has to live in mass, plane breaks and pose — knee spread, elbow width, where the widest horizontal line sits — or the pair collapses into one skull with two haircuts.

ranked_risks.risk: Black-on-black collapse: the dinner suit becomes a silhouette-shaped hole in a dark venue
ranked_risks.why: The jacket is the largest surface on the character and the reference's own solution is unavailable to River. Measured reference black sits at sRGB 13 with identical values on the lit chest and the shadowed flank; it only reads because it is cut against an sRGB 131 backdrop. River's venue is dark, so there is no borrowed backdrop and no guaranteed rim from every seat angle. Nothing about the tailoring — lapel roll, button stance, waist suppression, cuff — survives if the cloth carries no form.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Set the material contract before any garment geometry is authored: cloth floored at sRGB 55-65 (~4-5% reflectance), body cloth roughness 0.65-0.75 against facing/braid/bow at 0.15-0.25, a barathea weave in normal and roughness tuned against the actual table-camera texel density, heavy baked AO at armhole, lapel roll, collar underside, welt, buttonhole and hem, plus a wool sheen/Fresnel term so the shoulder and outer arm self-rim without a scene light. Validate by screenshotting the seated figure on the real venue lighting rig with the backdrop removed.

ranked_risks.risk: Doll eyes survive the geometry fix and return through the shader
ranked_risks.why: The face reader calls untinted white sclera plus a fully visible iris with no upper-lid shadow the reference's clearest failure, and the fix is split across two disciplines — lid aperture, globe recession and lid thickness are mesh; sclera tint, occlusion and catchlight are material. A correctly sized socket still reads doll-like with a pure white eyeball, so a half-fix scores as no fix. Eyes are also the one feature the preview bust frames largest.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Treat it as one deliverable, not two. Lower the aperture until the upper lid crosses the top of the iris at neutral with no sclera above it, shrink the iris slightly, set the globe back with a defined lateral orbital rim, give the lids visible wet-line thickness — then in the same pass tint the sclera off-white with a warm inner corner, bake upper-lid contact occlusion onto the eyeball, and fix a catchlight policy against the table key. Sign off on both together at the preview-bust framing, never on the geometry alone.

ranked_risks.risk: The hair shell still reads as a painted cap at the 35-40 degree preview framing
ranked_risks.why: This is a bug River already has, and the reference has it too, so there is nothing to copy the fix from. The hair reader identifies three independent mechanisms — a stair-stepped straight front edge, a shell cut on a plane rather than conformed to the skull (which is what opens the bald temple gap), and zero transition zone where hair meets skin. Fixing only the hairline height, the most tempting single change, leaves all three intact. And unlike the reference, River puts a camera on the hairline in the character-preview bust and the winner close-up.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Fix all three or none: rebuild the front edge as an M/bell in plan (no straight run over a quarter of the forehead width, no corner radius under 30mm, tuft offset 3-5mm off centre), shrinkwrap the shell to the head at 2-4mm offset so it terminates on the side plane with a continuous sideburn in front of the tragus, and paint a stubble/shadow gradient 10-15mm past the mesh edge at ~35% falling to zero. Gate on a 35-40 degree render: if the hair silhouette falls inside the skull silhouette on the far side, it is still a cap.

ranked_risks.risk: Hand scale set wrong, in either direction, and then propagated into the rig and props
ranked_risks.why: This is the only place two readers give opposite build directions for the same part — body says the reference hand is undersized at 0.55-0.60 head height and must grow strongly; seated says it is oversized, spanning nearly the full head width, and must shrink. Their targets almost coincide (~0.75-0.80 head height, or wrist-crease to middle fingertip equal to chin-to-hairline), so the disagreement is about the reference frames, not about River. But it is a poker game: hands hold the cards, cut the chips, and are the closest thing to camera on every hand played. A scale error is visible continuously and, once the rig, grip poses, card fan width and chip stack diameter are built on it, expensive to reverse.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Do not take a direction from either reader. Build the hand to the agreed absolute — wrist crease to middle fingertip equal to chin-to-hairline, palm width 0.8 of palm length — measured in Blender against River's own finished head, and lock that number before rigging. Only then set the card, chip and rail prop scales from it.

ranked_risks.risk: Reading male by widening, with three separate 'slight' increases stacking into a superhero
ranked_risks.why: Lateral width is the fastest path to caricature and it is the reference's own error, but the compounding is the subtler danger: the body reader asks for a strong gender macro plus increased shoulder breadth, the tailoring reader asks for a squarer shoulder with 1-1.5cm extension past the deltoid and a slight body-breadth increase, and the seated reader asks for slightly more deltoid mass. Each is defensible alone; applied independently by different passes they land far outside the 3.0-3.2 head-width cap the body reader set, and the jacket's construction adds apparent width on top of all of it.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Make biacromial span a single budgeted number owned by one pass — 3.0-3.2 head-widths bare — and treat the jacket's shoulder extension as spending from that budget, not adding to it. Get the male read from chest depth (0.95-1.0 head-heights), a narrowed pelvis so the shoulder overhangs the hip, a trap/deltoid plane break and neck mass. Hold the muscle macro low; a Bond lead is skeletal breadth and tailoring, not hypertrophy.

ranked_risks.risk: Jaw, chin and cheek judged with cover the character does not have
ranked_risks.why: Every bearded reference frame is load-bearing — the one clean-shaven closeup exposes a mandible that reads markedly narrower and a chin markedly smaller than the bearded frames implied. The same trap operates with hair: a shell that covers the temples flatters a forehead with no plane definition. River's lead is clean-shaven with short hair and fully exposed ears, so there is no cover anywhere on the head.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Evaluate the jaw, chin, cheek and forehead only on the bare mesh, with the hair asset hidden, at every checkpoint. Use the SQUARED/WEAK preset pair as an explicit silhouette bracket: if River's outline can be mistaken for either, it is wrong. Add a jaw-shadow/stubble tone in texture as a deliberate description of the mandible, decided after the geometry is signed off, never as a rescue for it.

ranked_risks.risk: Seated pose failures — hovering, folding at the waist, thigh through the rail
ranked_risks.why: Seated is essentially the entire game, and the three classic tells all show at the default seat camera: hands resting on the rail plane but floating above it, buttocks not deforming the cushion, soles not fully on the floor; a bend at the waist instead of the femoral head, which kills the weight read; and, with only 60-80mm of knee-to-rail clearance, a low-poly thigh with linear skinning punching through the rail underside before the lean-in extreme is reached. A lumbar sculpted straight while standing also turns into a visible slump the moment he sits.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Set the neutral against a true orthographic side view — 12-15 degrees from vertical, hinge at the hip, zero waist flexion, downhill femur — and validate by silhouette relationships (knee below rail, wrist past the inner roll, ear over acromion), never by tracing angles off the reference's raised-orbit frames. Author sleeve contact deformation where the forearm crosses the rail edge, cushion and sole contact, and test the lean-in extreme for thigh/rail collision before the pose set is accepted.

ranked_risks.risk: Silver and gold converge into the same figure
ranked_risks.why: They share a skeleton, a pipeline and — per the body reader's stated constraint — a base height, which removes segment length as a channel. If the difference is then left to the gender macro plus costume, the two read as one skull with different hair, and every localised delta paid for is wasted.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Spend the dimorphism budget deliberately in the two remaining channels. Mass: male limb circumference against female at roughly 70-75%, shoulder clearly overhanging the hip versus hers at or barely outside it, shallower female trap slope, plus localised brow, chin, malar and neck deltas rather than macro alone. Pose: his knees abducted ~12 degrees a side with elbows outside the ribcage so the widest horizontal line sits at the shoulder-elbow band; hers knees near-parallel and elbows tucked so hers sits at the hip. Never reuse one seated pose for both.

ranked_risks.risk: MPFB2 morph stacking overshoot, and the age macro quietly undoing the jaw
ranked_risks.why: Several jaw and chin targets combine non-linearly and blow past the intended silhouette when applied together. Separately, reaching for the age macro to get late-thirties adds sag and jowl across the whole head and will erode exactly the gonial corner and cheek structure that were just built.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Apply one morph at a time and check the outline against the SQUARED/WEAK bracket after each. Keep the age macro around 0.40-0.45 and deliver the age through specific features — faint tear-trough, faint modelled nasolabial form, slightly receded temples — then re-check the jaw corner after the macro is set, not before.

ranked_risks.risk: Detail authored for a closeup that does not survive the table camera, and detail skipped that does
ranked_risks.why: River has two framings with opposite demands: the poker camera resolves only the outer silhouette and the largest value shapes, while the preview bust and winner close-up resolve the hairline, the eye and the hands. Effort routinely goes to micro-forms that vanish at distance while the load-bearing items — jaw corner, brow shadow, neck-to-jaw separation, the white pocket square, the trouser braid, the cuff points — are treated as polish.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Split the checklist by camera and check both every session. Table camera: silhouette and the largest value breaks. Close camera: hairline transition, eye shading, hand and wrist junction. Anything that changes the outline — lapel roll, bow tie, pocket square, trouser break — must be geometry; cuff buttons and welts can be maps.

ranked_risks.risk: Head scale drift once the head is parented to the body
ranked_risks.why: A head authored in isolation routinely ends up oversized on the full figure, and the readers disagree about whether the reference head is already slightly oversized or is the thing the reference gets most right — so there is no safe default to fall back on. The failure only shows on the seated figure at the real camera.
ranked_risks.mitigation: Fix the figure at 7.75-8.0 head-heights and verify head scale only on the full seated figure at the actual game camera. Resist enlarging the head to fix table-distance readability; solve that with silhouette and value contrast.

contradictions: Hand scale, direction reversed: the body reader measures the reference hand at 0.55-0.60 of head height and calls for a STRONG INCREASE to 0.75-0.80; the seated reader measures it as spanning nearly the full cheek-to-cheek head width and calls for a MODERATE DECREASE. Their absolute targets nearly coincide (~0.75-0.80 head height / wrist crease to middle fingertip equal to chin-to-hairline), so the conflict is an artefact of the frames — a standing wardrobe shot versus a hands-beside-face closeup where the hands are nearer camera. Do not average, and do not take a slider direction from either. Set the absolute against River's own head and measure.

Neck circumference, direction reversed, and the readers also disagree about the reference itself: the face reader says the reference neck is 'nearly as wide as the jaw' and calls for a MODERATE DECREASE; the body reader measures it at 0.65-0.70 of bigonial width and calls for a MODERATE INCREASE to 0.75-0.80. Both agree the visible column must lengthen and that a submandibular shelf is missing. The 0.75-0.80 bigonial target happens to satisfy the face reader's 'clearly narrower than the jaw' as well, so a single number resolves the intent — but the sign of the MPFB2 change is genuinely undetermined and must be settled by measuring the neutral human, not by trusting either reading of the reference.

Neck column length: the face reader targets roughly half a head-height of visible column and explicitly warns that past about half it goes uncanny and breaks the dinner-jacket collar fit when seated. The body reader targets 0.55-0.60 head-heights — above the face reader's stated ceiling. Build at 0.50-0.55 and check the collar fit in the seated pose before going higher.

Wrist narrowing, same intent, incompatible numbers: the body reader wants the wrist at roughly 60% of the forearm's widest circumference; the seated reader wants it narrowed by about 20%, i.e. roughly 80%. That is a wide spread for a junction that is on camera in every hand pose because the shirt cuff and link terminate there. Neither is derived from a measurement of River. Suggest ~0.70-0.75 and validate against the actual French cuff geometry.

Collar type: the tailoring reader specifies a turndown collar with shorter points and more spread, and explicitly rejects a wing collar as reading 'waiter, not Bond' at game scale. The body reader twice justifies neck dimensions by reference to 'a wing collar and bow tie'. Tailoring owns this decision; the neck targets stand regardless, but the justification in the body reading should not be allowed to reintroduce the wing collar.

Head scale: the face reader says the head reads slightly oversized against the torso and asks to shave a few percent. The body reader says the small head is 'the single thing the reference gets most right', is what keeps the figure out of bobblehead territory, and treats any head-scale change as a caricature risk. Both land near 7.75-8.0 head-heights, so the practical gap is small — but they disagree about which direction the error lies in, so this must be judged on the full seated figure rather than adjusted on either reader's word.

Forearm budget: the body reader wants the forearm lengthened (to bring fingertips to true mid-thigh) and tapered with a brachioradialis swell. The seated reader says spend nothing on the forearm because River's silver is sleeved to the wrist and the forearm silhouette is cloth. These are reconcilable — length and the wrist taper affect the sleeve and the cuff landing, surface muscle description does not — but the reconciliation has to be stated, or one pass will model anatomy nobody sees while another skips the length correction that the reach depends on.

Internal inconsistency in the body reading (worth flagging because it will be copied): it says River should 'go slightly further than the reference' on shoulder-to-waist taper, then targets 0.68-0.70, which sits inside the reference's own measured 0.65-0.72 band and is looser than its low end. The defensible part of that observation is not the ratio but the taper's starting height — from the lower pectoral rather than from the belt. Take the start point, treat the ratio as unconstrained by the reference.

Shoulder width is requested three times from three levers and never reconciled: body (macro breadth increase, capped at 3.0-3.2 head-widths), tailoring (squarer shoulder line plus 1-1.5cm extension past the deltoid, plus a slight body-breadth increase), seated (slight deltoid mass increase). Each says 'slight'; applied independently they stack past the cap. One owner, one number.

Forehead: the hair reader says leave forehead vertical scale at neutral and fix the hair edge, not the head — warning that shortening the forehead to compensate for a badly placed hairline displaces the brow and breaks the skull. The face reader wants substantial forehead work. These are compatible only if the forehead change is strictly plane definition (frontal eminences, temporal ridge, slight backward rake) with no vertical rescale. Stated so it is not read as licence to reproportion the forehead.
gaps: Skin value and complexion are unspecified by every reader. The tailoring reader floors the jacket at sRGB 55-65 partly on the argument that it still reads black 'next to skin', but no reading sets the skin's albedo, and in a dark venue the face is the primary read and the only large light-value surface above the shirt. Skin tone, its value separation from both the white shirt and the black cloth, and its behaviour under the table key need to be decided alongside the garment contract, not after it.

No poly budget, texel density, camera FOV or view distance is stated anywhere, yet several deltas are unresolvable without them: the weave tiling that 'survives the target texel density', the AO bake resolution, the 12-20 alpha card ring at the hairline, and the repeated judgement about what 'survives at poker-table distance'. These numbers are prerequisites, not details.

Chair and rail dimensions are River's, not the reference's, but the entire seated geometry is specified against the reference's furniture — rail height, seat pan height, the 60-80mm knee clearance, the wrist clearing the inner roll. If River's table and chair differ at all, the pose numbers move and the thigh/rail collision margin changes.

Which gold female parameters are already locked and therefore binding on silver is never established. The body reader asserts uniform base height as a 'binding River constraint' and no other reader mentions it. Shared skeleton, shared shader, shared texel density and shared rig targets all constrain silver in different ways and need to be enumerated before the first morph is applied.

Expression and the poker loop are absent. The face reader correctly rules that the confident mouth-corner set is a rig target and must never be baked into neutral — but nobody specifies the expression set the game actually needs (fold, call, bluff, win, loss reaction), how the wrinkle map delivers the glabella furrow on expression, or what the neutral has to blend cleanly into. Authoring a neutral without knowing its extremes is how neutrals end up unusable.

Hair behaviour under the poses the seated reader wants is uncovered. The chin-on-hand secondary idle is called the most character-carrying pose in the set, and it puts a hand into the jaw and near the hair shell; head turns at the table do the same. No reading addresses shell intersection, or whether the hair is rigid at all.

Footwear is orphaned. The tailoring reader mentions patent leather only as a warning against sharing the trouser material, and the seated reader wants soles flat with toes turned out 10-15 degrees — but no reader owns shoe geometry, and nobody establishes which cameras see below the rail at all. If none do, both those notes are wasted effort; if the preview bust is full-figure, the shoe is the brightest black on the character.

Stubble and jaw-shadow policy for a clean-shaven late-thirties male is missing from the face reading, though the hair reader independently invents it for the hairline. It is the cheapest available way to describe a mandible with no facial hair to hide behind — but it must be decided after the geometry is signed off, and the rule for that ordering is not written anywhere.

There is no asymmetry budget. Three readers separately ask for asymmetry — subtle brow/nasal deviation, a frontal tuft offset 3-5mm with one recession marginally deeper, asymmetric hand placement — with no single owner or ceiling. Uncoordinated, these either cancel out or compound into something that reads as injury or as a modelling error.

Nobody defines the acceptance framings except in passing. The hair reader alone invokes the character-preview bust and the winner close-up; the others reason mostly from the table camera. The full list of framings the character must pass, and which checklist applies to each, does not exist and should be written before the build starts.

The waistcoat/cummerbund question is raised once by the tailoring reader and never resolved. It materially changes the torso read when he is seated and the jacket falls open — it is the difference between a bright shirt stripe with two undefined black wings and a banded midsection — and it also changes the neck, collar and button-stance decisions downstream.

consolidated_deltas.parameter: Jacket cloth base reflectance (floor the black)
Roughness split between body barathea (0.65-0.75) and satin facing, braid, bow and button covers (0.15-0.25)
Authored seam ambient occlusion — armhole, lapel roll turn-under, collar underside, welt, buttonhole, hem, waistband, hem-to-shoe contact
Cloth weave micro-detail in normal and roughness, tiled against the real table-camera texel density
Wool sheen / Fresnel self-rim on shoulder, upper arm and lapel edge (no reliance on a scene rim or a bright backdrop)
Eye lid aperture height — upper lid crosses the top of the iris at neutral, no sclera above
Eye socket depth and orbital recession, with a defined lateral orbital rim so the outer corner sits in shadow
Eye shading contract — sclera tinted off pure white, upper-lid contact occlusion baked onto the globe, catchlight policy fixed against the table key
Iris and overall eye scale (fix apparent narrowness by shrinking, not by moving)
Interocular spacing — hold at one eye-width, five eye-widths across the head at eye level, verified by measurement after the size change
Hairline plan shape — replace the straight stair-stepped edge with an M/bell: no straight run over a quarter of the forehead width, no corner radius under 30mm, tuft offset 3-5mm off centre
Temple coverage — close the bald gap; hair continuous around the temple corner and down in front of the tragus as a tapered sideburn
Hairline transition zone — stubble/shadow gradient painted 10-15mm past the mesh edge at ~35% falling to zero, optionally a 12-20 card ring overlapping the shell edge by ~5mm
Hair shell conformance — shrinkwrap to the skull at 2-4mm offset, terminating on the side plane rather than cut on a plane

Hand overall scale — wrist crease to middle fingertip equal to chin-to-hairline (~0.75-0.80 head height). Readers give opposite signs; set the absolute by measurement against River's own head before rigging
consolidated_deltas.direction: contested — set by measurement, not by slider sign

consolidated_deltas.parameter: Palm width relative to palm length (~0.8, long rather than square)
Finger taper proximal to distal (~15%) with small swells at PIP and DIP
Wrist circumference relative to forearm maximum (~0.70-0.75; readers say 0.60 and 0.80) plus a readable ulnar head
Knuckle and dorsal tendon relief — four resolvable MCP heads, two to three extensor ridges that surface only on extension
Chin projection forward, until the chin point sits on or just ahead of the lower-lip line in profile
Chin width — narrow to a defined button with a shallow mental crease
Gonial corner definition as a plane change, corner level with or slightly above the earlobe
Jaw width at the gonion — 0.90-0.95 of temple width, well inside the SQUARED bound
Brow ridge projection (enough to shadow the upper lid under a key)
Brow slab continuity — heavy over the inner third, thinning and rolling back laterally; no painted glabella furrow at neutral
Nasion depth (scoop between brow and nasal root)
Forehead plane definition — frontal eminences plus temporal ridge, plus slight backward rake. Plane change only: do not rescale forehead height
Zygomatic forward projection (forward, not wider), with a shallow hollow beneath and the masseter brought back up in front of the ear
